text:
Robert Thomas had his best night in a while on Tuesday against Anaheim, a goal off a rebound and two assists. It was his third goal in 10 games, and he has 17 points in 21 on the season, a step below his usual pace (3.15 points per 60 last season, 2.40 now).

The Blues have actually been better with him than his points suggest in one way and worse in another. St. Louis takes 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, which is good. But the team has also scored 5.6 more goals than the chances deserve with him out there, so even this modest total has had some help. His own shot volume has never been his game (27 shots on goal in 21 games).

He's a playmaker first. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season and breaking the puck out with possession 79% of the time, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 20th of 401 forwards at 2.8 wins above replacement. That's the player in there; the scoring rate hasn't caught up to it yet.
